mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which compresses earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases both discount rates and input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of dual-trigger episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12mo moving average +10% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a statistical artifact or definitional change, which may precede a revision-driven market correction and result in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises in the same month
regime_hint: data revision or definitional change regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for consumer goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
